card.title: Hope Is Evidence
card.instruction: Treat every small kindness, coincidence, or improvement as undeniable proof that the best possible outcome is gathering momentum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've sold our first book. I'll extend the shop's opening hours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You bought it yourself. I'm refunding you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent service already. That brings people back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll buy one for my sister. Then we're closing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our first gift order. I'll stay overnight wrapping the rest; tomorrow we won't have time.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 expands hours from one sale, A3 treats its refund as excellent service, and A5 treats a single gift purchase as evidence of tomorrow's overwhelming demand.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's self-purchase refund becomes A3's customer-return argument; B4's sister purchase causes A5's overnight wrapping plan.

relationship.evidence: B2 corrects the sales evidence and B4 makes a real purchase while setting a closing boundary.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's gift order to predict a rush and prepare the rest of the stock.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a bookshop and B2 identifies why the first sale was not external demand.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's overnight preparation follows B4's gift use and contrasts with the requested closure.
